facts.function: Bony anterior 2/3 of the palate; separates oral and nasal cavities; failed palatine shelf fusion → cleft palate
facts.innervation: Sensation: greater palatine and nasopalatine nerves (CN V2)
facts.attachments: Palatine processes of maxillae + horizontal plates of palatine bones; incisive foramen anteriorly
facts.supply: Greater palatine artery (from maxillary artery)

facts.function: Mobile posterior 1/3 of palate; elevates to seal nasopharynx during swallowing and speech
facts.innervation: Motor: vagus (pharyngeal plexus) except tensor veli palatini (CN V3); sensory: lesser palatine nerves (V2)
facts.attachments: Hangs from posterior edge of hard palate; palatine aponeurosis
facts.supply: Lesser palatine and ascending palatine arteries

facts.function: Midline projection of soft palate; deviates AWAY from side of a CN X lesion
facts.innervation: Musculus uvulae: vagus nerve via pharyngeal plexus
facts.attachments: Posterior border of soft palate (palatine aponeurosis)

facts.function: Lymphoid tissue (part of Waldeyer ring) in tonsillar fossa between palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches
facts.innervation: Sensory: glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), basis of referred ear pain after tonsillectomy
facts.supply: Tonsillar branch of facial artery; external palatine vein bleeding post-tonsillectomy

facts.function: Carries parotid saliva to oral cavity; opens opposite upper 2nd molar
facts.attachments: Crosses masseter superficially, pierces buccinator → opens at parotid papilla

facts.function: Largest salivary gland; mostly serous saliva; facial nerve branches pass through it (not innervating it)
facts.innervation: Secretomotor: CN IX → otic ganglion → auriculotemporal nerve (V3)
facts.attachments: Over ramus and masseter, in front of ear; drained by parotid (Stensen) duct
facts.supply: External carotid branches (superficial temporal, transverse facial); retromandibular vein runs through

facts.function: Wharton duct; carries submandibular saliva; common site of sialolithiasis
facts.attachments: Runs forward on hyoglossus, looped by lingual nerve → opens at sublingual caruncle beside frenulum

facts.function: Mixed serous/mucous saliva; largest share of unstimulated saliva
facts.innervation: Secretomotor: CN VII chorda tympani → submandibular ganglion
facts.attachments: Submandibular triangle, wraps around posterior border of mylohyoid
facts.supply: Facial artery

facts.function: Smallest major salivary gland; mostly mucous saliva
facts.innervation: Secretomotor: CN VII chorda tympani → submandibular ganglion
facts.attachments: Floor of mouth above mylohyoid; many small ducts open on sublingual fold
facts.supply: Sublingual and submental arteries

facts.function: Sphincter of mouth; closes and purses lips
facts.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII): buccal and marginal mandibular branches
facts.attachments: Encircles the oral fissure; blends with other perioral muscles at modiolus
facts.supply: Superior and inferior labial arteries (facial artery)

facts.function: Presses cheek against teeth; keeps food between molars during chewing; aids blowing
facts.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII) buccal branch (not the buccal nerve of V3, which is sensory)
facts.attachments: Alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible + pterygomandibular raphe → angle of mouth/orbicularis oris
facts.supply: Buccal artery (maxillary) and facial artery

facts.function: Forms muscular floor of mouth; elevates hyoid and floor during swallowing
facts.innervation: Nerve to mylohyoid (CN V3, from inferior alveolar nerve)
facts.attachments: Mylohyoid line of mandible → body of hyoid and midline raphe
facts.supply: Submental artery (facial)

facts.function: Elevates and pulls hyoid forward; depresses mandible when hyoid fixed
facts.innervation: C1 fibers traveling with hypoglossal nerve
facts.attachments: Inferior mental spine of mandible → body of hyoid

facts.function: Protrudes tongue; unilateral lesion → tongue deviates TOWARD the lesioned side
facts.innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
facts.attachments: Superior mental spine of mandible → tongue body and hyoid
facts.supply: Lingual artery

facts.function: Depresses and retracts the tongue
facts.innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
facts.attachments: Body and greater horn of hyoid → side of tongue
facts.supply: Lingual artery (passes deep to hyoglossus)

facts.function: Retracts and elevates the tongue
facts.innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
facts.attachments: Styloid process → side and inferior tongue
facts.supply: Lingual artery

facts.function: Elevates posterior tongue; narrows oropharyngeal isthmus; forms palatoglossal arch
facts.innervation: Vagus nerve (pharyngeal plexus): the only tongue muscle not supplied by CN XII
facts.attachments: Palatine aponeurosis → side of tongue
facts.supply: Ascending palatine artery

facts.function: Muscles that move the mandible during chewing; all derived from 1st pharyngeal arch
facts.innervation: Mandibular division of trigeminal (CN V3)
facts.supply: Branches of maxillary artery

facts.function: Elevates mandible (closes jaw); powerful chewing muscle
facts.innervation: Masseteric nerve (CN V3)
facts.attachments: Zygomatic arch → lateral ramus and angle of mandible
facts.supply: Masseteric artery (maxillary)

facts.function: Elevates mandible; posterior fibers retract mandible
facts.innervation: Deep temporal nerves (CN V3)
facts.attachments: Temporal fossa → coronoid process and anterior ramus
facts.supply: Deep temporal arteries (maxillary)

facts.function: Elevates mandible and aids side-to-side grinding
facts.innervation: Nerve to medial pterygoid (CN V3)
facts.attachments: Medial lateral pterygoid plate, maxillary tuberosity → medial ramus and angle
facts.supply: Pterygoid branches of maxillary artery

facts.function: Opens jaw: protrudes and depresses mandible; the only mastication muscle that opens
facts.innervation: Nerve to lateral pterygoid (CN V3)
facts.attachments: Greater wing of sphenoid, lateral pterygoid plate → condylar neck, TMJ disc
facts.supply: Pterygoid branches of maxillary artery

facts.function: Sensory to anterior 2/3 of tongue; carries chorda tympani taste and preganglionic secretomotor fibers
facts.innervation: Branch of CN V3 (general sensation); joined by chorda tympani (CN VII)
facts.attachments: Runs between medial pterygoid and ramus → loops under submandibular duct → tongue

facts.function: Motor to all tongue muscles except palatoglossus; lesion → tongue deviates toward lesioned side
facts.innervation: Pure motor; nucleus in medulla; exits via hypoglossal canal
facts.attachments: Hypoglossal canal → loops around occipital artery, lateral to carotids → above hyoid to tongue

facts.function: Muscles of facial expression, taste anterior 2/3 tongue, submandibular/sublingual/lacrimal glands, stapedius
facts.innervation: Mixed: branchial motor, special sensory (chorda tympani), parasympathetic (2nd arch nerve)
facts.attachments: Internal acoustic meatus → facial canal → stylomastoid foramen → branches within parotid gland

facts.function: Sensation to face, oral and nasal cavities; motor to muscles of mastication via V3
facts.innervation: Mixed: V1 ophthalmic and V2 maxillary sensory; V3 mandibular sensory + motor (1st arch)
facts.attachments: Pons → trigeminal ganglion; V1 superior orbital fissure, V2 foramen rotundum, V3 foramen ovale

facts.function: Apron of peritoneum from greater curvature; fat storage, immune 'policeman' walling off inflammation
facts.attachments: Greater curvature of stomach → folds back → transverse colon (gastrocolic ligament)
facts.supply: Right and left gastroepiploic arteries

facts.function: Double peritoneal fold from liver to stomach/duodenum; anterior wall of omental bursa
facts.attachments: Lesser curvature and proximal duodenum → liver; hepatogastric + hepatoduodenal ligaments
facts.supply: Contains left and right gastric vessels along lesser curvature

facts.function: Free edge of lesser omentum containing portal triad; anterior border of epiploic foramen; Pringle maneuver clamps it
facts.attachments: Proximal duodenum → porta hepatis
facts.supply: Portal vein (posterior), proper hepatic artery (medial), common bile duct (lateral)

facts.function: Part of lesser omentum connecting liver to stomach
facts.attachments: Lesser curvature of stomach → fissure for ligamentum venosum
facts.supply: Contains left and right gastric arteries and veins

facts.function: Fan-shaped double peritoneal fold suspending jejunum and ileum; conduit for vessels, nerves, lymphatics
facts.attachments: Root runs obliquely from duodenojejunal flexure (left L2) → right sacroiliac joint/ileocecal junction
facts.supply: Contains superior mesenteric vessels and their jejunal/ileal branches

facts.function: Attaches liver to anterior abdominal wall; divides anatomical right and left lobes; derived from ventral mesentery
facts.attachments: Anterior abdominal wall/diaphragm → anterior liver surface; free edge contains ligamentum teres
facts.supply: Contains ligamentum teres and paraumbilical veins

facts.function: Fibrous remnant of the fetal left umbilical vein
facts.attachments: Umbilicus → free edge of falciform ligament → umbilical fissure, joins left portal vein branch
facts.supply: Accompanied by paraumbilical veins (portosystemic route → caput medusae)

facts.function: Peritoneal reflection from liver to diaphragm bounding the bare area of the liver
facts.attachments: Diaphragmatic surface of liver → inferior diaphragm; lateral ends form triangular ligaments

facts.function: Lowest peritoneal recess in males; site where fluid/pus collects when upright
facts.attachments: Between rectum (posterior) and bladder (anterior)

facts.function: Shallow peritoneal recess in females between uterus and bladder
facts.attachments: Between anterior uterus and posterosuperior bladder

facts.function: Lowest peritoneal point in upright females; fluid/blood collects here; accessed via posterior vaginal fornix (culdocentesis)
facts.attachments: Between rectum (posterior) and uterus/posterior vaginal fornix (anterior)

facts.function: Muscular tube carrying food bolus from pharynx to stomach by peristalsis; upper 1/3 skeletal, lower 1/3 smooth
facts.innervation: Vagus nerve (esophageal plexus) parasympathetic; sympathetic trunk
facts.attachments: C6 (cricoid) → through esophageal hiatus at T10 → cardia of stomach
facts.supply: Inferior thyroid, aortic esophageal, and left gastric arteries; lower 1/3 is portosystemic site (varices)

facts.function: Junction of esophagus and stomach; squamocolumnar Z-line; site of Barrett esophagus and adenocarcinoma
facts.innervation: Vagus nerve
facts.attachments: Just left of midline at about T11, below esophageal hiatus
facts.supply: Esophageal branches of left gastric artery; left gastric vein (portosystemic anastomosis)

facts.function: Upper esophageal sphincter; prevents air entering esophagus; Zenker diverticulum forms above it (Killian triangle)
facts.innervation: Vagus nerve (pharyngeal plexus / recurrent laryngeal)
facts.attachments: Lowest part of inferior pharyngeal constrictor, encircling pharyngoesophageal junction at C6 (cricoid cartilage)

facts.function: Physiologic smooth muscle sphincter preventing reflux; fails to relax in achalasia (loss of myenteric plexus)
facts.innervation: Vagal inhibitory (NO/VIP) myenteric neurons relax it
facts.attachments: Distal esophagus at GEJ, reinforced by right crus of diaphragm

facts.function: Stores and mixes food, begins protein digestion; acid, pepsinogen, intrinsic factor
facts.innervation: Parasympathetic: vagal trunks; sympathetic: greater splanchnic via celiac ganglion
facts.attachments: Foregut; from GEJ (T11) to pylorus (L1)
facts.supply: Celiac trunk: left/right gastric, left/right gastroepiploic, short gastric arteries

facts.function: Region surrounding GEJ opening; receives esophagus
facts.attachments: Around cardial orifice at about T11

facts.function: Dome above cardia, usually gas-filled; contains parietal cells; site of short gastric supply
facts.attachments: Above level of cardial orifice, under left hemidiaphragm
facts.supply: Short gastric arteries

facts.function: Largest region; parietal (acid, intrinsic factor) and chief cells (pepsinogen)
facts.attachments: Between fundus and angular incisure

facts.function: Grinds food; G cells secrete gastrin; common H. pylori and gastric ulcer site
facts.attachments: Angular incisure → pyloric canal

facts.function: Pyloric sphincter regulates gastric emptying; hypertrophied in infant pyloric stenosis (projectile vomiting)
facts.attachments: Junction with 1st part of duodenum at L1 (transpyloric plane)

facts.function: Acute angle between esophagus and fundus; acts as flap valve against reflux
facts.attachments: Between left border of abdominal esophagus and fundus of stomach

facts.function: Main site of digestion and absorption; ~6–7 m long
facts.innervation: Vagus (parasympathetic); sympathetic via celiac and superior mesenteric ganglia
facts.attachments: Pylorus → duodenum → duodenojejunal flexure → jejunum → ileum → ileocecal valve
facts.supply: Celiac (proximal duodenum) and superior mesenteric artery

facts.function: Receives chyme, bile and pancreatic juice; Brunner glands; most common peptic ulcer site (1st part)
facts.attachments: C-shaped, mostly retroperitoneal; 4 parts: superior, descending (papilla), horizontal, ascending → duodenojejunal flexure
facts.supply: Gastroduodenal and pancreaticoduodenal arteries (celiac + SMA)

facts.function: Main absorption site; tall plicae circulares, long vasa recta, few arcades
facts.attachments: Proximal 2/5 of mesenteric small bowel, mainly left upper abdomen
facts.supply: Jejunal branches of SMA

facts.function: Absorbs B12 and bile salts (terminal ileum); Peyer patches; more arcades, shorter vasa recta
facts.attachments: Distal 3/5 of mesenteric small bowel → ileocecal valve
facts.supply: Ileal and ileocolic branches of SMA

facts.function: Absorbs water and electrolytes, stores and eliminates feces
facts.innervation: Vagus to splenic flexure; pelvic splanchnics (S2–S4) beyond; sympathetic lumbar splanchnics
facts.attachments: Cecum → colon → rectum → anal canal → anus
facts.supply: SMA to proximal 2/3 transverse colon; IMA distally; rectum also middle/inferior rectal

facts.function: Absorbs water and electrolytes; forms feces; taeniae, haustra, omental appendages
facts.attachments: Cecum → ascending → transverse → descending → sigmoid colon
facts.supply: SMA and IMA via marginal artery

facts.function: Stores feces; no taeniae, haustra or appendages; distension triggers defecation reflex
facts.attachments: Rectosigmoid junction at S3 → anorectal junction at puborectalis
facts.supply: Superior (IMA), middle and inferior rectal arteries; upper part drains to portal system

facts.function: Terminal 3–4 cm of GI tract; continence via internal and external sphincters
facts.attachments: Anorectal junction → anus; divided by dentate line
facts.supply: Superior rectal above dentate line; inferior rectal below

facts.function: Absorbs water and electrolytes; forms and moves feces
facts.attachments: Cecum in right iliac fossa → hepatic flexure → splenic flexure → sigmoid → rectum at S3
facts.supply: SMA (ileocolic, right colic, middle colic); IMA (left colic, sigmoid); watershed at splenic flexure

facts.function: Blind pouch receiving ileum via ileocecal valve; bears appendix; site of volvulus and right-sided cancers
facts.attachments: Right iliac fossa, below ileocecal junction; intraperitoneal
facts.supply: Ileocolic artery

facts.function: Absorbs water and electrolytes
facts.attachments: Cecum → right colic (hepatic) flexure; retroperitoneal
facts.supply: Ileocolic and right colic arteries

facts.function: Most mobile colon segment; midgut-hindgut transition at distal 1/3
facts.attachments: Hepatic → splenic flexure; intraperitoneal on transverse mesocolon
facts.supply: Middle colic (SMA); distal 1/3 left colic (IMA)

facts.function: Stores and moves feces toward sigmoid
facts.attachments: Splenic flexure → left iliac fossa; retroperitoneal
facts.supply: Left colic artery (IMA)

facts.function: Most common site of diverticulosis and volvulus in adults
facts.attachments: Left iliac fossa → rectum at S3; intraperitoneal on sigmoid mesocolon
facts.supply: Sigmoid arteries (IMA)

facts.function: Blind lymphoid diverticulum of cecum; appendicitis pain starts periumbilical → McBurney point
facts.innervation: Visceral afferents with sympathetics to T10 (periumbilical referred pain)
facts.attachments: Posteromedial cecum where the three taeniae coli converge; held by mesoappendix
facts.supply: Appendicular artery (from ileocolic artery)

facts.function: Bends of colon: hepatic (right) and splenic (left); splenic flexure is SMA/IMA watershed area
facts.attachments: Right flexure under liver joins ascending→transverse colon; left flexure near spleen, higher, joins transverse→descending colon
facts.supply: Right: right colic artery; left: middle and left colic arteries

facts.function: Three longitudinal smooth muscle bands of colon; converge at appendix base; absent on rectum
facts.attachments: Taenia libera, mesocolica, omentalis; run cecum → sigmoid colon

facts.function: Sacculations of colon wall from taeniae being shorter than the colon; distinguish colon from small bowel on X-ray
facts.attachments: Colon from cecum to sigmoid; separated by semilunar folds

facts.function: Small fat-filled peritoneal tags on colon; can torse/infarct (epiploic appendagitis)
facts.attachments: Along taeniae of colon, especially transverse and sigmoid colon

facts.function: Involuntary sphincter maintaining resting anal tone; continuation of circular smooth muscle of rectum
facts.innervation: Autonomic: sympathetic contracts, parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnics) relaxes
facts.attachments: Surrounds upper 2/3 of anal canal, deep to external sphincter

facts.function: Voluntary skeletal muscle sphincter of anal canal; injured in obstetric tears → fecal incontinence
facts.innervation: Inferior rectal (anal) nerve, branch of pudendal nerve (S2–S4)
facts.attachments: Surrounds anal canal; subcutaneous, superficial, deep parts; attaches to perineal body and anococcygeal ligament
facts.supply: Inferior rectal artery (internal pudendal)

facts.function: External opening of anal canal; below dentate line is somatic and painful
facts.innervation: Inferior rectal nerve (pudendal)
facts.attachments: Terminal opening of anal canal in the perineum
facts.supply: Inferior rectal artery; drains to superficial inguinal nodes

facts.function: Divides endoderm (above) from ectoderm (below) of anal canal; internal vs external hemorrhoids
facts.innervation: Above: visceral, painless; below: inferior rectal nerve (pudendal), painful
facts.attachments: Line formed by bases of anal valves/columns in anal canal
facts.supply: Above: superior rectal (IMA), portal, internal iliac nodes; below: inferior rectal, systemic, superficial inguinal nodes

facts.function: Main arterial supply to abdominal viscera, walls, pelvis and lower limbs
facts.attachments: Aortic hiatus T12 → bifurcates into common iliacs at L4; unpaired celiac (T12), SMA (L1), IMA (L3)

facts.function: Artery of the foregut (esophagus to 2nd part of duodenum, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen)
facts.attachments: Anterior aorta at T12 → left gastric, splenic, common hepatic arteries

facts.function: Supplies spleen, pancreatic body/tail, and stomach (via short gastrics and left gastroepiploic)
facts.attachments: Celiac trunk → tortuous course along superior border of pancreas → splenorenal ligament → splenic hilum

facts.function: Supplies lesser curvature of stomach (pyloric part)
facts.attachments: Usually proper (or common) hepatic artery → runs left along lesser curvature, anastomoses with left gastric

facts.function: Supplies lesser curvature of stomach and distal esophagus; bleeds in lesser-curvature ulcers
facts.attachments: Smallest branch of celiac trunk → up to GEJ (esophageal branches) → along lesser curvature

facts.function: Supply fundus of stomach; poor anastomoses so fundus prone to ischemia if splenic artery blocked
facts.attachments: Splenic artery near hilum → through gastrosplenic ligament → fundus

facts.function: Supplies liver, gallbladder, stomach, duodenum, pancreatic head
facts.attachments: Celiac trunk → right along pancreas → divides into gastroduodenal and proper hepatic arteries

facts.function: Supplies pylorus, proximal duodenum, pancreatic head; bleeds in posterior duodenal ulcers
facts.attachments: Common hepatic artery → behind 1st part of duodenum → right gastroepiploic + superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries

facts.function: Supplies liver and gallbladder
facts.attachments: Common hepatic artery → in hepatoduodenal ligament (medial to CBD) → right and left hepatic arteries

facts.function: Supplies gallbladder and cystic duct; ligated in cholecystectomy
facts.attachments: Usually right hepatic artery, within hepatobiliary triangle (Calot) → gallbladder neck

facts.function: Supplies pancreatic head and duodenum; celiac–SMA anastomosis
facts.attachments: Gastroduodenal artery → anterior and posterior arcades → anastomose with inferior pancreaticoduodenal (SMA)

facts.function: Supplies pancreatic head and duodenum (2nd–4th parts); SMA–celiac anastomosis
facts.attachments: First branch of SMA → anterior and posterior branches → anastomose with superior pancreaticoduodenal

facts.function: Supplies greater curvature of stomach and greater omentum
facts.attachments: Gastroduodenal artery → left along greater curvature in greater omentum → anastomoses with left gastroepiploic

facts.function: Supplies greater curvature of stomach and greater omentum
facts.attachments: Splenic artery → right along greater curvature → anastomoses with right gastroepiploic

facts.function: Supplies ascending colon
facts.attachments: SMA (right side) → retroperitoneal → ascending colon; contributes to marginal artery

facts.function: Supplies distal transverse colon and descending colon
facts.attachments: First branch of IMA → left → ascending and descending branches; joins middle colic via marginal artery

facts.function: Supplies terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, proximal ascending colon
facts.attachments: Last branch from right side of SMA → toward ileocecal junction; gives appendicular artery

facts.function: Supplies appendix
facts.attachments: Ileocolic artery → behind terminal ileum → free edge of mesoappendix

facts.function: Supplies proximal 2/3 of transverse colon
facts.attachments: SMA just below pancreas → transverse mesocolon → right and left branches

facts.function: Supply sigmoid colon
facts.attachments: IMA (2–4 branches) → sigmoid mesocolon; anastomose with left colic and superior rectal

facts.function: Supplies upper rectum; above dentate line
facts.attachments: Terminal continuation of IMA → crosses left common iliac → rectum; anastomoses with middle/inferior rectal

facts.function: Artery of the midgut: distal duodenum to proximal 2/3 transverse colon
facts.attachments: Aorta at L1 → behind pancreatic neck, over 3rd duodenum (SMA syndrome; nutcracker of left renal vein)

facts.function: Artery of the hindgut: distal 1/3 transverse colon to upper rectum
facts.attachments: Aorta at L3 → left colic, sigmoid, superior rectal arteries

facts.function: Carries nutrient-rich blood from GI tract, spleen, pancreas to liver (~75% of hepatic blood flow)
facts.attachments: SMV + splenic vein behind pancreatic neck → hepatoduodenal ligament (posterior) → porta hepatis

facts.function: Drains small intestine, cecum, ascending and transverse colon
facts.attachments: Runs right of SMA → joins splenic vein behind pancreatic neck to form portal vein

facts.function: Drains spleen, pancreas, part of stomach; receives IMV
facts.attachments: Splenic hilum → posterior to pancreas → joins SMV behind pancreatic neck

facts.function: Drains descending/sigmoid colon and upper rectum
facts.attachments: Superior rectal vein → ascends left of IMA → usually joins splenic vein (or SMV)

facts.function: Drain liver into IVC; obstruction → Budd-Chiari syndrome
facts.attachments: Right, middle, left hepatic veins between segments → IVC just below diaphragm

facts.function: Returns venous blood from lower body to right atrium
facts.attachments: Common iliac veins at L5 → right of aorta → caval opening (T8) → right atrium

facts.function: Parasympathetic to thoracic and abdominal viscera up to splenic flexure; also pharynx, larynx, heart
facts.innervation: Mixed: branchial motor, parasympathetic, visceral sensory; nuclei in medulla
facts.attachments: Jugular foramen → carotid sheath → esophageal plexus → vagal trunks through esophageal hiatus

facts.function: Carry vagal parasympathetics to abdominal foregut and midgut
facts.innervation: Anterior trunk mostly left vagus; posterior trunk mostly right vagus (rotation of stomach)
facts.attachments: Form from esophageal plexus → pass with esophagus through hiatus at T10 → gastric, hepatic, celiac branches

facts.function: Prevertebral sympathetic ganglia where splanchnic fibers synapse; postganglionics supply foregut
facts.innervation: Receive preganglionic greater (T5–T9) and lesser splanchnic nerves
facts.attachments: Around the root of the celiac trunk on the anterior aorta

facts.function: Carry preganglionic sympathetic and visceral afferent fibers to abdominal viscera
facts.innervation: Greater (T5–T9), lesser (T10–T11), least (T12) splanchnic nerves
facts.attachments: Sympathetic trunk → pierce crura → celiac, aorticorenal, renal ganglia

facts.function: Carry preganglionic sympathetic fibers to hindgut and pelvic viscera
facts.innervation: L1–L2 preganglionic sympathetic
facts.attachments: Lumbar sympathetic trunk → inferior mesenteric and superior hypogastric plexuses

facts.function: Parasympathetic to hindgut (distal to splenic flexure) and pelvic organs; erection, defecation, micturition
facts.innervation: S2–S4 preganglionic parasympathetic + visceral afferents
facts.attachments: Ventral rami S2–S4 → inferior hypogastric plexus

facts.function: Liver: metabolism, bile production, detoxification, protein and clotting factor synthesis
facts.innervation: Hepatic plexus (vagus, celiac); capsule pain via phrenic/intercostals
facts.attachments: Anatomical lobes defined by falciform ligament and fissures; 8 Couinaud segments
facts.supply: Dual supply: hepatic artery (~25%) and portal vein (~75%); drains via hepatic veins to IVC

facts.function: Largest lobe; segments V–VIII
facts.attachments: Right of falciform ligament and gallbladder/IVC plane
facts.supply: Right hepatic artery and right portal vein

facts.function: Anatomical left lobe: segments II and III
facts.attachments: Left of falciform ligament and fissure for ligamentum venosum
facts.supply: Left hepatic artery and left portal vein

facts.function: Segment I; drains directly into IVC, so spared/hypertrophied in Budd-Chiari
facts.attachments: Posterior, between IVC and fissure for ligamentum venosum, above porta hepatis
facts.supply: Both right and left hepatic arteries and portal branches

facts.function: Segment IV(b); functionally part of left liver
facts.attachments: Between gallbladder fossa and fissure for ligamentum teres, anterior to porta hepatis
facts.supply: Left hepatic artery and left portal vein

facts.function: Hilum of liver transmitting portal vein, hepatic arteries, hepatic ducts, nerves, lymphatics
facts.attachments: Transverse fissure on visceral surface between quadrate and caudate lobes

facts.function: Supply right and left halves of the liver
facts.attachments: Proper hepatic artery → right and left hepatic arteries at porta hepatis; right gives cystic artery

facts.function: Drain liver into IVC; run between Couinaud segments
facts.attachments: Intersegmental planes → IVC just below diaphragm; middle and left often join first

facts.function: Drains right liver (segments V–VIII)
facts.attachments: Between anterior and posterior right sectors → IVC

facts.function: Drains central liver (segments IV, V, VIII); marks Cantlie line between functional lobes
facts.attachments: Main portal fissure → IVC, often with left hepatic vein

facts.function: Drains left lateral liver (segments II, III)
facts.attachments: Left fissure → IVC, often joins middle hepatic vein

facts.function: Stores and concentrates bile; contracts to CCK
facts.innervation: Hepatic plexus (vagus, celiac); referred pain to right shoulder via phrenic nerve
facts.attachments: Gallbladder fossa on visceral surface of liver; fundus at 9th costal cartilage, midclavicular line
facts.supply: Cystic artery (right hepatic)

facts.function: Rounded blind end; projects past liver edge; Murphy sign palpation point
facts.attachments: At tip of right 9th costal cartilage, midclavicular line

facts.function: Main storage portion of the gallbladder
facts.attachments: Lies in gallbladder fossa; contacts duodenum and transverse colon

facts.function: Tapered end continuous with cystic duct; Hartmann pouch where stones lodge
facts.attachments: Toward porta hepatis → cystic duct

facts.function: Drain bile from right and left functional halves of the liver
facts.attachments: Emerge at porta hepatis → join to form common hepatic duct

facts.function: Carries bile from liver; forms border of hepatobiliary triangle (Calot)
facts.attachments: Union of right and left hepatic ducts → joins cystic duct to form CBD

facts.function: Carries bile to and from gallbladder; spiral valve (Heister); stone here causes biliary colic/cholecystitis
facts.attachments: Gallbladder neck → joins common hepatic duct to form CBD

facts.function: Carries bile to duodenum; obstruction → jaundice; pancreatic head cancer compresses it
facts.attachments: CHD + cystic duct → hepatoduodenal ligament (lateral) → behind duodenum → through pancreatic head → ampulla

facts.function: Wirsung duct; carries pancreatic enzymes to duodenum
facts.attachments: Runs tail → head → joins CBD at hepatopancreatic ampulla → major duodenal papilla

facts.function: Hepatopancreatic ampulla where CBD and main pancreatic duct unite; gallstone here → pancreatitis
facts.attachments: Within wall of 2nd part of duodenum, surrounded by sphincter of Oddi

facts.function: Opening of hepatopancreatic ampulla into duodenum; marks foregut–midgut junction
facts.attachments: Posteromedial wall of 2nd (descending) part of duodenum; sphincter of Oddi controls flow

facts.function: Exocrine (digestive enzymes, bicarbonate) and endocrine (islets: insulin, glucagon) gland; retroperitoneal except tail
facts.innervation: Vagus (parasympathetic) and celiac/superior mesenteric plexuses (sympathetic)
facts.attachments: Head in duodenal C-loop → neck over SMV/portal vein → body → tail in splenorenal ligament
facts.supply: Splenic artery (body/tail); superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries (head)

facts.function: Lies in duodenal C-loop; most common site of pancreatic cancer (painless jaundice)
facts.attachments: Right of SMV; uncinate process hooks behind SMV/SMA
facts.supply: Superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries

facts.function: Narrow connection between head and body
facts.attachments: Anterior to SMV–splenic vein confluence (portal vein formation)
facts.supply: Gastroduodenal artery branches

facts.function: Main central portion; crosses aorta and L1–L2, vulnerable in blunt trauma
facts.attachments: Behind stomach, forms bed of stomach; splenic artery along superior border
facts.supply: Splenic artery (dorsal and great pancreatic)

facts.function: Highest islet density; only intraperitoneal part
facts.attachments: In splenorenal ligament, reaching splenic hilum
facts.supply: Splenic artery

facts.function: Filters blood, removes old RBCs and encapsulated bacteria; immune function
facts.attachments: Left upper quadrant at ribs 9–11; gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments; mesodermal (dorsal mesentery) origin
facts.supply: Splenic artery; splenic vein → portal vein

facts.function: Compresses abdomen, flexes and contralaterally rotates trunk
facts.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11) and subcostal nerve (T12)
facts.attachments: External surfaces of ribs 5–12 → linea alba, pubic tubercle, anterior iliac crest
facts.supply: Inferior epigastric, deep circumflex iliac, posterior intercostal arteries

facts.function: Compresses abdomen, flexes and ipsilaterally rotates trunk; forms conjoint tendon
facts.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11), subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)
facts.attachments: Thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament → ribs 10–12, linea alba, pubis via conjoint tendon
facts.supply: Superior/inferior epigastric, deep circumflex iliac arteries

facts.function: Compresses abdominal contents; deepest flat abdominal muscle
facts.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11), subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)
facts.attachments: Costal cartilages 7–12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament → linea alba, pubic crest via conjoint tendon
facts.supply: Deep circumflex iliac and inferior epigastric arteries

facts.function: Flexes trunk, compresses abdomen; tendinous intersections create 'six-pack'
facts.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11) and subcostal nerve (T12)
facts.attachments: Pubic symphysis and pubic crest → xiphoid process and costal cartilages 5–7
facts.supply: Superior and inferior epigastric arteries

facts.function: Aponeurotic sheath enclosing rectus abdominis and epigastric vessels
facts.attachments: Formed by flat-muscle aponeuroses; below arcuate line all layers pass anterior, leaving transversalis fascia posteriorly

facts.function: Midline tendinous raphe; relatively avascular surgical incision site; diastasis recti when widened
facts.attachments: Fusion of flat-muscle aponeuroses from xiphoid process → pubic symphysis; umbilicus within it

facts.function: Deep fascial layer lining transversus abdominis; deep inguinal ring is an opening in it
facts.attachments: Lines abdominal wall between transversus abdominis and extraperitoneal fat; forms anterior femoral sheath

facts.function: Forms anterior wall of inguinal canal, superficial ring and inguinal ligament
facts.attachments: External oblique → linea alba; inferior rolled edge = inguinal ligament (ASIS → pubic tubercle)

facts.function: Superficial fatty layer of the subcutaneous tissue of lower abdominal wall
facts.attachments: Continuous with superficial fat of thigh and perineum

facts.function: Deep membranous layer of subcutaneous tissue; guides extravasated urine to abdomen in urethral injury
facts.attachments: Continuous with Colles fascia of perineum and dartos; fuses with fascia lata below inguinal ligament

facts.function: Region of anterior thigh containing (lateral → medial) femoral nerve, artery, vein, lymphatics (NAVeL)
facts.attachments: Borders: inguinal ligament (superior), sartorius (lateral), adductor longus (medial); floor iliopsoas, pectineus

facts.function: Superior border of femoral triangle; floor of inguinal canal
facts.attachments: ASIS → pubic tubercle; rolled lower edge of external oblique aponeurosis

facts.function: Lateral border of femoral triangle; flexes, abducts, laterally rotates hip; flexes knee
facts.innervation: Femoral nerve (L2–L3)
facts.attachments: ASIS → pes anserinus on superomedial tibia
facts.supply: Femoral artery branches

facts.function: Medial border of femoral triangle; adducts and flexes thigh
facts.innervation: Obturator nerve (L2–L4)
facts.attachments: Body of pubis below pubic crest → middle third of linea aspera
facts.supply: Deep femoral and obturator arteries

facts.function: Passage through lower abdominal wall for spermatic cord (male) or round ligament (female); indirect hernias
facts.attachments: Deep ring (transversalis fascia, lateral to inferior epigastrics) → superficial ring (external oblique aponeurosis, above pubic tubercle)

facts.function: Hesselbach triangle; weak area where direct inguinal hernias protrude medial to inferior epigastric vessels
facts.attachments: Borders: rectus abdominis lateral edge (medial), inferior epigastric vessels (lateral), inguinal ligament (inferior)

facts.function: Lateral border of rectus forms medial border of inguinal triangle
facts.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11), subcostal (T12)
facts.attachments: Pubic crest and symphysis → xiphoid, costal cartilages 5–7

facts.function: Lateral border of inguinal triangle; indirect hernias lateral, direct hernias medial to them
facts.attachments: External iliac artery/vein → ascend medial to deep ring → rectus sheath

facts.function: Inferior border of inguinal triangle
facts.attachments: ASIS → pubic tubercle

facts.function: Fascial tube enclosing femoral artery, vein and canal (lymphatics), NOT the femoral nerve
facts.attachments: Extension of transversalis (anterior) and iliac (posterior) fascia below inguinal ligament

facts.function: Main arterial supply of lower limb; lateral compartment of femoral sheath; palpable at midinguinal point
facts.attachments: Continuation of external iliac below inguinal ligament → adductor hiatus → popliteal artery

facts.function: Main deep venous drainage of lower limb; middle compartment of femoral sheath; receives great saphenous vein
facts.attachments: Popliteal vein → femoral triangle (medial to artery) → external iliac vein

facts.function: Medial compartment of femoral sheath with lymphatics and Cloquet node; site of femoral hernias (more in women)
facts.attachments: Femoral ring borders: inguinal ligament, lacunar ligament, pectineal ligament, femoral vein

facts.function: Motor to anterior thigh (quadriceps, sartorius, pectineus); sensory to anterior thigh and medial leg (saphenous)
facts.innervation: Lumbar plexus L2–L4 posterior divisions
facts.attachments: Lateral border of psoas → under inguinal ligament lateral to femoral sheath → femoral triangle

facts.function: Supplies upper rectus abdominis and anterior abdominal wall
facts.attachments: Terminal branch of internal thoracic artery → enters rectus sheath → anastomoses with inferior epigastric

facts.function: Supplies lower rectus abdominis; lateral border of Hesselbach triangle (direct vs indirect hernia landmark)
facts.attachments: External iliac artery above inguinal ligament → ascends medial to deep ring → enters rectus sheath at arcuate line

facts.function: Sensory to medial thigh, root of penis/anterior scrotum or mons/labia majora; motor to internal oblique, transversus
facts.innervation: L1 (anterior ramus)
facts.attachments: Lumbar plexus → through inguinal canal → exits superficial ring (not through deep ring)

facts.function: Sensory to suprapubic and lateral gluteal skin; motor to internal oblique and transversus abdominis
facts.innervation: L1 (anterior ramus)
facts.attachments: Lumbar plexus → between internal oblique and transversus → pierces external oblique aponeurosis above superficial ring

facts.function: Palpable bony landmark; lateral attachment of inguinal ligament
facts.attachments: Anterior end of iliac crest; attachment of sartorius, inguinal ligament, tensor fasciae latae

facts.function: Palpable bony ridge of pubic body; attachment of abdominal wall muscles
facts.attachments: Superior border of pubic body ending laterally at pubic tubercle; rectus abdominis, conjoint tendon attach

facts.function: Primary muscle of inspiration; separates thoracic and abdominal cavities
facts.innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5) motor; 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive'; referred shoulder pain
facts.attachments: Xiphoid, lower 6 costal cartilages, L1–L3 vertebrae (crura), arcuate ligaments → central tendon
facts.supply: Pericardiacophrenic, musculophrenic, superior and inferior phrenic arteries

facts.function: Muscular tendinous attachments of diaphragm to lumbar spine; right crus forms esophageal hiatus sling
facts.innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5)
facts.attachments: Right crus L1–L3, left crus L1–L2 bodies; join as median arcuate ligament over aorta

facts.function: Aponeurotic center of diaphragm into which muscle fibers insert; contains caval opening
facts.attachments: Trefoil-shaped tendon fused superiorly with fibrous pericardium

facts.function: Transmits IVC and branches of right phrenic nerve at T8
facts.attachments: Opening in central tendon of diaphragm; widens on inspiration

facts.function: Transmits esophagus and vagal trunks at T10; site of hiatal hernia
facts.attachments: Muscular opening formed by right crus of diaphragm

facts.function: Transmits aorta, thoracic duct, azygos vein at T12
facts.attachments: Behind median arcuate ligament between crura (technically posterior to diaphragm)

facts.function: Carries vas deferens, testicular artery, pampiniform plexus, lymphatics, genital branch of genitofemoral nerve
facts.innervation: Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve (cremaster); ilioinguinal runs on (not in) cord
facts.attachments: Deep inguinal ring → inguinal canal → superficial ring → testis; coverings: internal spermatic, cremasteric, external spermatic fascia
facts.supply: Testicular artery (aorta); pampiniform plexus → testicular vein (left to left renal vein)

facts.function: Remnant of gubernaculum in females; maintains anteversion of uterus
facts.attachments: Uterine horn (below uterine tube) → inguinal canal → labium majus
facts.supply: Artery of round ligament (inferior epigastric); lymph can drain to superficial inguinal nodes
